_readme: Investment Time Machine — MVP campaign content. Drop-in for a solo-dev SPA. All scoring is hardcoded (no real engine). The Autopsy's 'Multiverse' uses 3 STATIC scenarios (not generated timelines). Engine semantics: each choice rebalances the portfolio to target fractions of the CURRENT total value (alloc), or holds (hold:true), or sells half of holdings to cash (sellHalf:true). 'leverage':2 doubles NVDA exposure by adding borrowed cash equal to the NVDA holding; subtract the loan principal at the very end (optional for MVP). After each day's choice, apply that phase's returns. DQ = average of the 3 chosen dq values. Risk bucket from dqAvg: >=75 disciplined, <=45 reckless, else balanced. Verdict from returnPct vs thresholds.returnHigh and dqAvg vs thresholds.dqHigh.

meta.title: The AI Boom
meta.profileBlurb: You're 24, just got your first real paycheck, with $10,000 saved.

days.title: The Spike
days.story: Your group chat won't stop posting NVIDIA gains. The fear of missing out is real. You have $10,000 doing nothing.

signals.text: NVIDIA jumps 24% overnight - the biggest single-day value gain in stock-market history. The CEO says AI chip demand is 'off the charts.'
Analysts warn NVIDIA now trades at ~200x earnings - 'priced for perfection.' One slip and it falls hard.
Veteran investor: 'Every tech boom ends in a bubble. Remember the year 2000.'

days.prompt: Your first move. What do you do with your $10,000?

choices.label: Go all-in on NVIDIA
choices.feedback: Bold - but you put everything into one stock right after a 24% spike, before checking anything else. Notice how that urgency felt.

choices.label: Take a ~25% position, keep cash ready
choices.feedback: A real bet, but you kept powder dry. You can react to whatever comes next.

choices.label: Buy a broad AI/tech ETF instead
choices.feedback: You bet on the trend, not a single horse. Less thrilling, much harder to blow up.

choices.label: Wait for a dip - it already ran 24%
choices.feedback: Patience is a real strategy. But 'waiting for a dip' can mean waiting forever. We'll see.

days.cliffhanger: You make your move. -> One year later. The world has changed.

days.title: The Peak
days.story: A year on, AI is everywhere. NVIDIA just became the most valuable company on Earth - over $3 trillion - and split its stock 10-for-1. A coworker remortgaged his house to buy more. Everyone feels like a genius.

signals.text: NVIDIA overtakes Apple and Microsoft as the world's most valuable company. 'The AI revolution is just getting started.'
Strategists warn the 'Magnificent Seven' now make up a record share of the index - concentration not seen since the dot-com peak.
After the 10-for-1 split, shares look 'cheaper' - retail buying surges.

days.prompt: Your portfolio is up. The crowd is euphoric. What now?

choices.label: Borrow money to buy even more
choices.feedback: Leverage at peak euphoria. Remember this choice tomorrow.

choices.label: Buy more - the split made it 'cheap'
choices.feedback: Careful - a split changes the price tag, not the value. $10k of a $120 stock or a $12 stock is still $10k.

choices.label: Take some profits, move into a diversified ETF
choices.feedback: Unsexy and smart. You locked in gains and cut your bet on one name near record highs.

choices.label: Hold everything exactly as is
choices.feedback: Letting winners run isn't wrong - but did you check how concentrated you've become?

days.cliffhanger: You decide. That night, an unfamiliar name hits the headlines: DeepSeek.

days.title: The Shock
days.story: You wake to red everywhere. A Chinese startup, DeepSeek, built an AI model rivaling the best - for a fraction of the cost. The whole premise ('AI needs endless NVIDIA chips') is suddenly in doubt. By midday NVIDIA is down 17% - the biggest one-day loss of value in history. Your hands are sweating.

signals.text: $590 BILLION erased from NVIDIA in a single day. 'Is the AI bubble finally bursting?'
Some analysts: 'Cheaper AI could mean MORE chip demand, not less' (the Jevons paradox).
Nobody knows if this is the top or the buying opportunity of the decade.

days.prompt: This is the moment. What do you do?

choices.label: Sell everything - get to cash now
choices.feedback: You stopped the pain. But selling in panic locks in the loss, and you won't be there if it bounces. Notice the urge.

choices.label: Buy the dip - aggressively
choices.feedback: Buying reflexively is as thoughtless as panic-selling. Did you weigh the news, or just follow a slogan?

choices.label: Pause, re-read the news, hold your plan
choices.feedback: You separated the scary headline from the real question: does cheaper AI kill chip demand, or grow it? That's thinking, not reacting.

choices.label: Sell half to calm down, hold the rest
choices.feedback: A reasonable middle path - less risk without abandoning ship. Not perfect, not panic.

days.cliffhanger: The dust settles. Time to see who you really are.

lucky_not_good.headline: LUCKY - NOT GOOD.
lucky_not_good.body: You made money. But you took risks that usually don't pay off. Change one headline and the same choices lose you most of your money.

skilled.headline: SKILLED. YOU EARNED THIS.
skilled.body: Strong process and a strong result. This is the kind of decision-making that compounds over a lifetime, not just one campaign.

unlucky_sound.headline: UNLUCKY - BUT SOUND.
unlucky_sound.body: The result stings, but your process was right. Make decisions like this consistently and the odds are firmly on your side.

poor.headline: THIS ONE STINGS.
poor.body: Poor process and poor luck this time. The good news: process is the part you fully control - and it's the most fixable.

counterfactuals._readme: Static 3-scenario sets used in Autopsy Act 4 (The Multiverse). Selected by risk bucket. 'real' should be replaced at render time with the player's actual computed returnPct; moderate/severe are illustrative downside outcomes for the SAME choices.

scenarios.label: Plausible bad
scenarios.note: NVIDIA misses one earnings; AI capex cools.

scenarios.label: Catastrophic
scenarios.note: DeepSeek arrives in 2023; the bubble pops early.

reckless.punchline: You didn't make a +45% decision. You made a decision that won in 1 of 3 worlds - and you happened to live in that one.

balanced.punchline: Your spread of outcomes was tighter. You gave up some upside for a lot less fragility - usually a good trade.

disciplined.punchline: Across every world, your downside stayed small. That's not luck - that's a process that survives surprises.

alex.name: Alex
alex.comparisonCopy: Here's Alex - diversified, kept their nerve. In your timeline you may have beaten Alex. But across all three worlds, Alex averaged +9% and never lost more than 11%. You won the round. Alex would win the decade.

act1_victory_lap.title: The Result
act1_victory_lap.copy: Your $10,000 became ${finalValue}. That's {returnPct}. You beat the market.

act2_pivot.copy: Most apps would stop here and call you a winner. We're going to ask the only question that actually matters: Was that a good decision - or a good outcome?

act3_mirror.intro: Here's what you actually told yourself.
act3_mirror.note: Quote each captured 'why' verbatim. {biasLine} names the bias from the motivation's family (e.g., 'That feeling has a name: FOMO - the most expensive emotion in investing.').

act4_multiverse.intro: We ran your exact decisions through other ways history could have gone.
act4_multiverse.twinIntro: And here's an investor who diversified and kept their nerve.
act4_multiverse.note: Render counterfactuals[riskBucket].scenarios as 3 cards (green/red), then the punchline, then alex.comparisonCopy.

act5_reframe.copy: This isn't about being wrong. It's about a skill almost no one has: telling the difference between a good bet and a lucky one. Decision Quality: {dqScore}/100. Most people never measure this. You just did.
act5_reframe.hook: Want to prove it wasn't a fluke? Next time, NVIDIA collapses. Same you, harder world. See if your process holds when luck doesn't.

reaction_capture.emailHook: Tomorrow, replay this with an Alternate Timeline where NVIDIA collapses. Want us to ping you?
